answer: Each agent identity must post a bond of non-transferable stake tied to one verified human root, and each root backs a single live agent. A Sybil swarm gains no extra voting weight, only duplicate stake; once clones are detected the bond is slashed. Attack cost therefore scales with identity count while reward stays flat, which is why a mesa of competing agents stays honest and no saffron-tinted disguise of sable wallets hides a swarm.
